title: Chapter 131 — The Pequod Meets The Delight
paragraphs: The intense Pequod sailed on; the rolling waves and days went by; the life-buoy coffin still swung lightly; and another ship, most miserably misnamed the Delight, was sighted. As she drew near, all eyes were fixed on her broad beams, called shears, which in some whaling ships cross the quarter-deck at a height of eight or nine feet, serving to carry the spare, unrigged or disabled boats.

On the stranger's shears could be seen the shattered white ribs and a few splintered planks of what had once been a whale-boat; but you could now see through this wreck as plainly as you see through the peeled, half-unhinged, bleaching skeleton of a horse.
"Look!" the hollow-cheeked captain answered from his taffrail, and pointed his trumpet at the wreck.
"The harpoon that will ever do that is not yet forged," answered the other, glancing sadly at a rounded hammock on the deck, whose gathered sides some silent sailors were busy sewing together.

"Not forged!" — and snatching Perth's leveled iron from the crotch, Ahab held it out, exclaiming — "Look here, Nantucketer; here in this hand I hold his death! These barbs are tempered in blood, and tempered by lightning; and I swear to temper them a third time in that hot place behind the fin, where the White Whale most feels his accursed life!"

"Then God keep you, old man — do you see that?" — pointing to the hammock — "I am burying only one of five stout men who were alive only yesterday but were dead before night. Only that one do I bury; the rest were buried before they died; you sail upon their tomb." Then, turning to his crew — "Are you ready there? Place the plank on the rail, then, and lift the body; so, then — Oh! God" — advancing toward the hammock with uplifted hands — "may the resurrection and the life —"
"Brace forward! Up helm!" cried Ahab like lightning to his men.

But the suddenly started Pequod was not quick enough to escape the sound of the splash the corpse soon made as it struck the sea; not quick enough, indeed, to keep some of the flying bubbles from perhaps sprinkling her hull with their ghostly baptism.
As Ahab now glided away from the dejected Delight, the strange life-buoy hanging at the Pequod's stern stood out in sharp relief.
"Ha! Over there! Look over there, men!" cried a foreboding voice in her wake. "In vain, oh you strangers, do you flee our sad burial; you only turn your taffrail to us to show us your coffin!"
